finding.claim: isJSONSerializable compares typeof result `t` to null instead of `value`, so null falls through and `value.buffer` throws TypeError instead of returning a boolean.
finding.title: isJSONSerializable crashes on null value due to wrong null check

repro.expectedBehavior: isJSONSerializable(null) returns true without throwing, since null is JSON-serializable and the early primitive branch was intended to return true for it.
repro.rationale: The buggy check `t === null` (typeof result compared to null) never matches, so null falls through to `value.buffer` and throws TypeError. Catching the throw and asserting no error plus result===true fails on the buggy code and passes when fixed.
repro.reason: assertion failed consistently on analyzed commit

finding.claim: Retry passes `...context.options` containing the already-aborted timeout signal, and the next attempt combines it with `AbortSignal.any`, so the retried fetch starts already aborted instead of with a fresh timeout.
finding.title: Timeout retry reuses aborted signal causing immediate abort

verifier.reason: Mutation at src/fetch.ts:171-178 stores the timeout/AbortSignal.any signal back into context.options.signal, and the retry at src/fetch.ts:71-75 spreads ...context.options into the next $fetchRaw call, so the next attempt re-enters src/fetch.ts:171-178 with an already-aborted signal and AbortSignal.any produces an already-aborted signal.
